about.title: Dorris Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Dorris is a quiet community along Rt 97 and 1st Street, and most people here don't expect a household appliance, farm equipment part, or vehicle component to fail and cause harm. But defective products don't discriminate by zip code. Whether the injury happened at home near N Main Street or out on 4th Street, California law gives injured people a real path to accountability. Product liability claims here often rest on strict liability, meaning the focus stays on whether the product itself was flawed rather than proving someone was careless. That distinction matters in a small town where the manufacturer or distributor may be based far away. Our team can review the product, the injury, and the facts, and explain what your options may be.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Dorris Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rule, you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which matters when the company that made the product isn't local to Siskiyou County.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact, rather than discarding or repairing it, can be critical evidence that supports a strict liability claim.

items.question: What counts as a product defect under California law?
items.answer: A defect generally falls into one of three categories: a design flaw that makes the product unsafe even when made correctly, a manufacturing error that occurred during production, or a failure to warn about a known risk. Any of these can support a strict liability claim if the defect caused your injury.

items.question: Does it matter that Dorris is a small town far from where the product was made?
items.answer: No. California strict liability law applies regardless of where you live, and manufacturers or distributors based outside Siskiyou County can still be pursued through the legal process. Our team can help identify who along the supply chain may be responsible.

items.question: What should I do with the product that caused my injury?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without cleaning, repairing, or discarding it. This preserved evidence can be important when evaluating whether a defect existed. If possible, also photograph it and note where you were, such as near 1st Street or N Main Street, when the injury occurred.

items.question: Is there a cost to get your help?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
